page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, numbered paragraphs set one under another. No marginal notes. A catchword at the lower right.

l.i: Et quin ipsi etiam conferat Philosophia, ecquid dubi-
tamus? cùm animum, ut contemplari aptissimè possimus,
perturbationibus ea liberet.
Est igitur Practica Philosophia, disciplina morum, ra-
tionem ostendens, qua mores ad virtutes componendi, ac
in rebus agendis ipsum summum hominis bonum sit ap-
prehendendum.
De eiusdem vero artificiosa constitutione & partibus
lis sanè multa est:nos autem animo sumus tranquillo.
Quæ[?] vero eiusmodi disciplinarū ratio est? Duas prin-
cipes invenio partes.
Prior in Finis & Summi boni expositione posita tota
est:posterior ea inquirit & interpretatur media, quibus
fine illo societas civilis possit beari.
Summum vero hominis bonum est actio Animi secũ-
dum virtutem optimam & perfectissimā, in vita quoq;
perfecta. Ethicor.7.
Cùm autem variæ definitionis Summi boni & intel-
ligantur & exprimantur partes; mirum non est, varias
quoq; tractationis illius in Morali Philosophia instituta,
effici partes.
Vel enim ipsa Virum bonum, ad quascunq; civiles so-
cietates obeundas, naturâ pronum, Virtutibus instruit
& informat.
Vel etiam in Rei familiaris convenienti administra-
tione praterea occupata est.

page.notes: The Roman numerals VII to XV are paragraph numbers, so they are set as paragraphs, not headings. "IIX." is printed that way and is kept as printed. The superscript reference mark after "perfecta" in XII has no matching note on the page and is left out. "Quæ" at the start of X is uncertain because the first letter is set in a special form. "praterea" in XV is printed without the ligature and is copied as seen. The page has no running head, page number or signature.
